title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: booking status for putting originals of a corrected set into circulation
content:
## Scope

When a corrected transport document of the Bills of Lading and Transport Documents product is issued as a new set, the status of the booking the document covers decides whether the cargo counts as on board for putting originals of that set into circulation.

## Formal clause

1. The booking counts as on board when it has the status loaded, departed or closed.
2. It also counts as on board when it has the status gated in, provided the document type's tier allows issuance once the cargo is gated in, before loading.
3. The booking read here is the booking record held by the documentation party of the document; a booking held by another customer is not read and counts as not on board.
4. Every other booking status counts as not on board.

## Quick check

| What the desk reads | Counts as on board? |
|---|---|
| Own booking record, status loaded, departed or closed | Yes |
| Own booking record, status gated in, tier permits issuance on gate-in | Yes |
| Own booking record, status gated in, tier does not permit issuance on gate-in | No |
| Own booking record, any other status | No |
| A booking record held by a different customer | Not read; not on board |

## Hypothetical cases

- The documentation party's booking shows closed at the moment the corrected set is issued: the booking counts as on board.
- The booking reference on the document leads to a booking of another customer that shows departed: it is not read, and the booking counts as not on board.

## Points of judgement

- **Question:** Is the booking status read at the moment of the original issue or of the corrected set? **Answer:** It is the booking record as it stands when the corrected set is issued.
- **Question:** Does a gated-in booking always count? **Answer:** Only on a tier that allows issuance once the cargo is gated in.
